summary: Four days of protests against corruption and one-party rule in Syria have resulted in at least four deaths and demonstrators setting fire to public buildings, posing the gravest domestic challenge yet to President Bashar al-Assad.
Syrian forces killed at least ten people in attacks on protesters in Deraa, including an assault on the Omari mosque complex and later gunfire on a solidarity march.
Secretary of State Hillary Clinton appeared to rule out U.S. military intervention in Syria, saying each Arab uprising was unique.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad gave his first speech since anti-government protesters took to the streets nearly two weeks earlier.
Syrian security forces killed 17 pro-democracy demonstrators in the southern city of Deraa as protests against President Bashar al-Assad flared in several towns.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad faces an unprecedented month-long wave of popular protests, responding with repression, economic handouts, and promises of reform.
Western powers have confined themselves to verbal outrage over the killing of some 350 people in Syria, prompting accusations of a double standard compared with military intervention in Libya.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's security establishment decided to wage war on protesters across the country, deploying tanks in Deraa as part of a crackdown that has killed more than 400 people.
Unrest sweeping Syria may whip up sectarian divisions that could spill across the border and threaten to destabilize Lebanon, according to analysts.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad is fighting for political survival amid a popular uprising that rights groups say has cost over 450 lives in six weeks.
The United States imposed sanctions on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad and other senior officials over the violent crackdown on pro-democracy protests.
Syria dropped its bid for an Arab slot on the U.N. Human Rights Council amid pressure over its crackdown on protesters, and Kuwait was elected instead.

The UK and France present a draft UN resolution condemning Syria's suppression of protests, stopping short of authorizing concrete action, as hundreds of Syrians flee into Turkey amid an expected crackdown.

Increasing numbers of refugees are moving from Syria into Turkey, fearing a major assault by the Syrian army and security agencies after the government said 120 security personnel were killed earlier this week.
Syrian tanks stormed the border town of Jisr al-Shughour overnight, prompting thousands of refugees to flee to Turkey, according to residents.

Almost 10,000 Syrians have fled to Turkey following a government crackdown on protesters, with protest organizers saying President Bashar al-Assad's campaign is responsible for the deaths of 1,300 civilians since mid-March.
Exiled Syrian opposition figures urged Russia to pressure President Bashar al-Assad to resign, while Russian officials met with Assad's critics in Moscow.

Syria's opposition remains united in demanding change but divided over strategy, with some backing dialogue with President Bashar al-Assad's authorities and others insisting he must leave, as the government granted a rare public platform to the opposition in Damascus while a crackdown on protests continued.
Syrian forces killed 24 civilians as tens of thousands of people called on President Bashar al-Assad to step down in some of the biggest demonstrations since a three-month uprising.

King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia demanded an end to the bloodshed against protesters in Syria and withdrew his ambassador to Damascus, but did not follow through with further measures against Syrian President Bashar al-Assad.
Saudi Arabia recalls its ambassador from Damascus in protest against Syria's deadly crackdown on anti-government demonstrators.
Gulf Arab states, including Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and Kuwait, recalled their envoys from Syria to rebuke President Bashar al-Assad's crackdown on unrest, deepening his international isolation.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad says he will not relent in pursuing "terrorist groups" despite Turkish FM Ahmet Davutoglu urging an end to military operations against civilian demonstrators.
The Syrian navy shelled the main Mediterranean port city of Latakia, as President Bashar al-Assad broadened a military offensive to crush street protests against his rule.
President Barack Obama, backed by the European Union, called for Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to leave power.

A European and U.S. draft resolution will call for U.N. Security Council sanctions against Syrian President Bashar al-Assad and several other top officials, and urges referring Syria's crackdown on protests to the International Criminal Court.
Syria faced Western and Arab condemnation at the U.N. Human Rights Council for its crackdown on anti-government protesters, with the U.N. reporting more than 2,200 people killed.

Syrian President Bashar al-Assad hosts Islamic leaders for an iftar meal in Damascus while activists say Syrian forces raided an eastern tribal region for a second day, extending a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.
A U.S. and European push to impose U.N. Security Council sanctions on Syria over its crackdown on pro-democracy demonstrators is meeting fierce resistance from Russia and China.
Syrian security forces attacked protesters at the al-Rifai mosque in Damascus, reportedly wounding the imam, amid unconfirmed reports of at least one death in clashes.
Arab League Secretary General Nabil al-Arabi is to visit Syria to try to resolve the crisis, carrying an initiative to solve the crisis, following a meeting of Arab foreign ministers in Cairo.
The EU banned imports of Syrian oil to increase pressure on President Bashar al-Assad's regime over its crackdown on anti-government protests.
Some Iraqis change travel plans from Syria to Iraq's Kurdish region due to bad security in Syria, where a government crackdown has killed 2,000 people according to the United Nations.

Syria's economy and port traffic have been heavily damaged by the popular uprising and international sanctions, with shipping volumes at Latakia and Tartous falling sharply and Iraqi traders seeking alternative routes.
Syrian army defectors began launching attacks on government forces, with loyalist forces attempting to wrest control of a central town from units that had gone over to the opposition.

Syria's main opposition groups form a National Council in Istanbul, calling on the international community to protect the Syrian people while rejecting foreign intervention that compromises Syria's sovereignty.
Turkey said it would impose sanctions on Syria despite the blocking of any U.N. measures against President Bashar al-Assad for his crackdown on dissent.
Turkey's military is to conduct a mobilization exercise in the southern province of Hatay, where more than 7,000 Syrians have taken refuge from Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's security forces.

Turkey increases pressure on Syria through border military exercises, planned economic sanctions, and sheltering Syrian opposition groups and army defectors, while seeking to avoid Arab suspicion or Syrian counter-measures.

Syrian security forces killed at least two people when they opened fire on tens of thousands of mourners at the funeral of Kurdish opposition figure Meshaal al-Tammo in Qamishli, which turned into an anti-Assad protest.

Syrian security forces shot dead three mourners and injured 20 when they fired on a protester funeral procession in central Damascus, while troops loyal to President Bashar al-Assad fought army defectors west of the capital.
Arab foreign ministers stopped short of suspending Syria from the Arab League over its military crackdown on dissent, instead urging the government and opposition to hold a dialogue within 15 days.
Turkey's foreign minister held his first acknowledged meeting with Syrian opposition leaders, urging peaceful means, as Syrian forces launched a major offensive in Homs.
The Arab League sent an urgent message to the Syrian government denouncing continued killings of civilians, as activists reported at least 37 protesters killed mostly in Homs and Hama.
Syria accepted an Arab League plan to pull the army out of cities and talk to its foes, but the plan was not implemented as the assault on Homs continued.
The Arab League suspends Syria and announces political and economic sanctions over President Bashar al-Assad's crackdown on protests.

Middle Eastern papers generally welcome the Arab League's decision to suspend Syria over its continued use of force against protesters, while some media outlets in Iran and China are sceptical about Western influence over the move.
The Arab League is expected to formally suspend Syria on Wednesday over its crackdown on protesters, as activists report at least 70 people killed on Tuesday alone.

The Arab League gave Syria three days to end its "bloody repression" or face sanctions, as Russia's foreign minister said the situation in Syria was beginning to resemble civil war after renegade soldiers attacked a key army base.
France recalled its ambassador to Damascus and Syria's suspension from the Arab League took effect, intensifying diplomatic pressure on President Bashar al-Assad over his crackdown on protests.
Russia stands by President Bashar al-Assad as Arab and Western countries seek to pressure the Syrian leader to halt a violent crackdown on his opponents.

Syria seeks changes to a planned Arab League monitoring mission on the eve of a deadline to comply with a peace initiative, as activists report 11 people killed and the Arab League threatens sanctions.

Turkish newspapers report that Ankara has contingency plans to create no-fly or buffer zones to protect civilians in neighboring Syria if the bloodshed worsens, while Turkey opposes unilateral steps or intervention aimed at regime change.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad says the crackdown on anti-government unrest will continue despite Arab League pressure and a deadline to comply with a peace plan.
The Arab League rejects Syria's demand to amend its peace plan for ending the country's conflict, as a deadline for Syria to end its crackdown passes with no sign of violence abating.

A UN panel reports that Syrian forces have committed crimes against humanity, including murder, torture, and sexual assault of civilians during the crackdown on the uprising against President Bashar al-Assad.

As Syria faces growing economic sanctions, diplomatic isolation, and UN condemnation over its crackdown on protesters, neighboring countries including Lebanon, Turkey, Iraq, and Jordan are closely watching the crisis and assessing potential impacts on their own interests.
Syrian President Bashar al-Assad grants a general amnesty for all crimes committed during the 10-month uprising, according to state-run media.

Syria's government firmly rejects Qatar's call for Arab troops to be deployed in the country to end the deadly crackdown on protesters, saying such a move would worsen the crisis and pave the way for foreign intervention.
The Arab League's monitoring chief warns of an escalation of violence in Syria as the government intensifies its crackdown on protests, with activists reporting 135 deaths in two days.
The Arab League suspends its observer mission to Syria, citing the critical deterioration of the situation and continued violence.

Russia's foreign ministry calls for talks between the Syrian authorities and the opposition and suggests Moscow as a venue, while Russia threatens to veto the latest UN Security Council resolution on Syria.
A UN Security Council debate on Syria ended without agreement, as China and Russia opposed an Arab League plan calling for an end to violence and for President Bashar al-Assad to stand down.
A Syrian and a German-Lebanese man were arrested in Berlin on suspicion of spying on opponents of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's government.

A revised UN Security Council draft resolution on Syria drops an explicit call for President Bashar al-Assad to hand over power, while Russia continues to send weapons to the Assad government despite the uprising.
Russia's deputy foreign minister says his country cannot support a draft UN Security Council resolution on Syria in its current form.
Russia and China veto an Arab League-inspired UN Security Council resolution on Syria, prompting Western criticism and straining relations with Moscow.
Russia and China veto a UN Security Council resolution supporting an Arab League peace plan for Syria, prompting Western accusations of complicity in the Assad regime's repression.
The Free Syrian Army is waging an escalating guerrilla war in Syria, with fighting and sectarian tensions reported in Homs and Qusayr.

Saudi Arabia circulates a draft resolution at the UN General Assembly calling for an end to violence in Syria and for President Bashar al-Assad to step aside, as Syrian forces continue to bombard Homs.
Al-Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahiri backed the anti-government uprising in Syria and urged militants in Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Turkey to support Syrian rebels.

Syrian security forces have stepped up military operations, including heavy weapons bombardment of residential areas in Homs, killing more than 400 people in less than a fortnight according to opposition activists.
Syria categorically rejects an Arab League resolution calling for a joint Arab-UN peacekeeping mission to end the country's 11-month conflict.
The UN General Assembly approves a non-binding resolution backing an Arab League plan that calls on Syrian President Bashar al-Assad to resign, a move Syria says will only worsen the crisis.
China sends Deputy Foreign Minister Zhai Jun to Damascus to seek a peaceful resolution to the Syria crisis.
The International Committee of the Red Cross says it is in talks with all concerned parties in Syria's conflict to negotiate a brief ceasefire to deliver aid to affected areas.
A United Nations panel delivers a list of Syrian officials, including possibly President Bashar al-Assad, who could be investigated for crimes against humanity.
China continues to oppose international action on Syria, blocking UN Security Council efforts and siding with Russia to shield the Assad regime from pressure.

The international community, including the Arab League, European Union, United States, and Turkey, has imposed wide-ranging sanctions on President Bashar al-Assad's regime in an attempt to pressure the Syrian government to stop using violence against demonstrators.

President Barack Obama rejects unilateral US military intervention in Syria, calling the situation "heartbreaking" but saying such action would be a mistake, while predicting that President Bashar al-Assad will fall.
Human Rights Watch reports that Syria is laying landmines along its borders, citing witness and deminer accounts, while the UN says 230,000 Syrians have fled their homes in the past year.
Kofi Annan says he is sending a team to Damascus to discuss setting up a new international monitoring mission for Syria.
Syrian activists express second thoughts about the peaceful movement as the uprising enters its second year and violence increases, with opposition figures divided over whether to take up arms.
A fierce firefight erupts in the al-Mezze district of Damascus, with machine-guns and rocket-propelled grenades heard, and Syrian TV reporting three "terrorists" and a security force member killed.
Russian President Dmitry Medvedev offered full support for UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan's peace mission in Syria, saying it may be the last chance to avoid a prolonged and bloody civil war.

Syrian forces stormed the rebel bastion of Qalaat al-Madiq in Hama province after a siege lasting more than two weeks, as the Arab League discussed a peace plan and Syria said it would not address any Arab League initiative.
UN-Arab League envoy Kofi Annan demands the Syrian government begin a ceasefire "now," saying the deadline for implementing his peace plan has passed.
Arab League summit in Baghdad formally supports a UN plan to end the fighting in Syria, though deep divisions remain over how to deal with the crisis.

An international summit in Istanbul, attended by Western and Arab leaders but boycotted by Russia, China, and Iran, sought to increase pressure on Syria over its failure to implement Kofi Annan's six-point peace plan, while Syria dismissed the meeting as the "enemies of Syria" and claimed victory over rebel fighters.
Kofi Annan briefs the UN Security Council on the progress of his peace plan for Syria as violence continues and Gulf Arab states agree to fund the rebel Free Syrian Army.
Syrian forces opened fire across the border into Turkey, prompting Turkey to summon Syria's envoy and demand an immediate halt to such violence, amid fading hopes for a UN-brokered ceasefire.
A UN-organised ceasefire between the Syrian government and anti-government rebel groups begins and appears to be holding with no reports of trouble so far.
The UN Security Council passes a resolution authorizing the deployment of an advance team of up to 30 unarmed monitors to Syria to oversee the ceasefire, as violence flares in Homs and Aleppo.

The Syrian government said "terrorist armed groups" escalated violence after the UN Security Council authorized the deployment of the first 30 truce observers, while opposition groups warned they could not remain committed indefinitely to an "empty truce" if the regime continued violations.
French Foreign Minister Alain Juppe says international sanctions against the Syrian government have cut its foreign currency reserves by half and warns Damascus is actively trying to evade sanctions.
Syrian security forces continue deadly attacks on opposition-held areas and bombard Homs despite a ceasefire, as UN observers begin their monitoring mission.

Syrian Foreign Minister Walid al-Muallim informs Kofi Annan in writing that provisions requiring the withdrawal of troops, tanks, and heavy weapons from population centres have already been carried out, despite much evidence to the contrary.
UN High Commissioner for Refugees Antonio Guterres says he believes events such as a deadly explosion in Hama will lead to an increased rate of refugees attempting to flee Syria.
An explosion in central Damascus kills at least 10 people and wounds 20, with Syrian state media blaming a suicide bomber and opposition activists blaming the government.
Vladimir Putin resists Western diplomatic pressure to support tougher action against Syria's government and calls for more time for Kofi Annan's peace plan.
A UN official says Syria is officially in full-scale civil war, with the government believed to have lost control of major cities to rebel fighters.
A UN official states that Syria is now in a state of civil war and the government has lost control of large chunks of cities.
The US says it is consulting international partners over next steps on Syria after UN observers suspended their activities due to escalating violence.

The head of UN observers in Syria urges warring parties to allow the evacuation of women, children, elderly and injured people from conflict zones, admitting attempts to extract civilians from Homs had been unsuccessful.

Continued shelling in Homs is preventing Red Cross teams from evacuating civilians despite a two-hour ceasefire agreed on Wednesday, while a Syrian fighter pilot lands in Jordan and requests political asylum.
Several high-ranking Syrian military figures, including a general and two colonels, defected to Turkey.

International diplomats meet in Geneva to try to revive Kofi Annan's six-point plan for a peaceful transition of power in Syria, though major powers remain divided over whether Bashar al-Assad should be excluded.

UN peace envoy Kofi Annan says there is international agreement that a transitional government should be set up in Syria , which could include both government and opposition members , while US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton says Syrian President Bashar al-Assad could not remain in power .

Wikileaks releases over 2 million emails from Syrian ministries and Baath party figures, dating from August 2006 to March 2012, with news stories based on the material to be published over the next two months.

More than 100 countries meeting in Paris as the Friends of Syria group called for tougher sanctions against Syria and urged Russia and China to end their support for President Bashar al-Assad's regime.
Kofi Annan and President Assad agreed to try to arrange localized ceasefires "from the ground up" in Syria.
Conflicting reports emerge about mass killings in Tremseh, Syria, with UN observers confirming heavy weapons were used but unable to determine the death toll or perpetrators.
The UN's Under-Secretary General for Peacekeeping Operations, Herve Ladsous, declares that Syria's deepening conflict has turned into a full-scale civil war.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov says Western attempts to get Moscow to discuss sanctions against Syria contain "elements of blackmail" and rejects calls for Russia to pressure President Bashar al-Assad to step down.
Syrian officials deny rebel claims of an all-out offensive in Damascus, saying security forces fought off attacks by small groups of armed terrorists.

Former Syrian ambassador to Iraq Nawaf Fares, the most senior diplomat to defect from Bashar al-Assad's regime, claims the Syrian government may have used chemical weapons in Homs and has colluded with al-Qaeda, though he offers no proof.
Fighting intensifies across Damascus as the military deploys tanks and helicopters, with rebel forces launching an all-out assault on the capital called Operation Damascus Volcano.

Defense Minister Daoud Rajiha and his deputy Assef Shawkat, President Assad's brother-in-law, are killed in a suicide attack during a high-level meeting at the national security headquarters, according to Syrian state TV.

The UN Security Council agrees to extend its observer mission in Syria for a final 30 days as up to 30,000 Syrian refugees are reported to have crossed into Lebanon over the past 48 hours amid intensified fighting.

The UN refugee agency is building a new camp in Jordan for Syrians fleeing the conflict, as UN and Red Crescent officials report a sharp increase in humanitarian needs with an estimated 1.5 million homeless people inside Syria.
The BBC's Ian Pannell reports traveling to the outskirts of Aleppo with hundreds, possibly a thousand, rebels as the battle for control of Syria's second city intensifies.

Syrian Kurds in northern Syria are asserting autonomy as the Assad regime pulls troops from peripheral areas for its assault on Aleppo, with the PYD reportedly controlling at least four main towns and cities.
The Syrian government intensified its aerial bombardment of Aleppo, while Western nations warned of a potential massacre and the UN urged Syria to halt its offensive.
Fresh clashes and helicopter gunship attacks are reported in Aleppo as the Syrian army offensive enters its fourth day, with thousands of refugees continuing to flee the city.
Nearly 150,000 Syrians have crossed into Jordan as fighting in Syria intensifies, prompting Jordan to rethink its response.
Fresh fighting is reported around Damascus and in Aleppo, where government forces bombard rebel-held areas and clashes occur in several districts.
Jordan moves a growing influx of displaced Syrians into a new tented city in the desert, the first official refugee camp, as Jordanian transit camps overflow with Syrian refugees.
The Arab League postpones a meeting in Saudi Arabia to debate the crisis in Syria and discuss a new envoy to replace Kofi Annan.
Syrian Prime Minister Riad Hijab defected from Bashar al-Assad's regime.

Syrian government forces launched a large operation to retake Aleppo from rebel fighters, with activists reporting fresh bombardment and the Free Syrian Army confirming a tactical withdrawal from the Salah al-Din district.
Amnesty International raises alarm over satellite images showing increased use of heavy weaponry and probable artillery impact craters near residential areas in Aleppo, Syria.

Syrian civilians are fleeing Aleppo in increasing numbers amid a lull in fighting between rebels and government forces, with the UN reporting almost 150,000 refugees registered in four neighboring countries.
Syria's Kurdish activists have begun to take control of towns near the border with Turkey, as analysts suggest Syria's Kurds could be among the winners from the political chaos in Syria.
Former Syrian PM Riad Hijab, who defected to Jordan the previous week, says the Syrian regime is collapsing "morally, financially and militarily" and does not control more than 30% of the territory.
China says it will receive Syrian presidential adviser Bouthaina Shaaban for talks with Foreign Minister Yang Jiechi as part of efforts to implement the UN's six-point peace plan.

Four Arab states urged their citizens to leave Lebanon amid signs that the conflict in Syria is spilling over into its western neighbor, and the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation suspended Syria's membership.
